use: A rule of natural justice: no one should be condemned without a hearing. Applied in Maneka Gandhi.

meaning: No one should be a judge in their own cause.
use: The rule against bias; a judge with a personal interest must step aside.

term: Actus non facit reum nisi mens sit rea
meaning: An act does not make a person guilty unless the mind is also guilty.
use: Most crimes need both a guilty act (actus reus) and a guilty mind (mens rea).

meaning: Ignorance of the law is no excuse.
use: You cannot escape liability by saying you did not know the law.

meaning: Ignorance of fact is an excuse.
use: A genuine mistake of fact in good faith can be a defence (BNS General Exceptions).
The same parties cannot litigate the same issue again once finally decided (Section 11, CPC).

meaning: Stand by what has been decided.
use: Courts follow earlier decisions; in India see Article 141.
The binding legal principle in a judgment.
Remarks in a judgment that are not essential to the decision; persuasive, not binding.

meaning: Where there is a right, there is a remedy.
use: The basis of Articles 32 and 226 and of tort law.

meaning: To a willing person, no injury is done.
use: A defence in tort when the claimant voluntarily accepted the risk.
In negligence, the facts can raise a presumption, e.g. surgical instruments left inside a patient.
Loss without violation of a legal right gives no claim (Gloucester Grammar School case).
Violation of a legal right is actionable even without loss (Ashby v White).

meaning: No one gives what they do not have.
use: A seller without title cannot pass good title, with some exceptions.
The buyer must check goods before buying; much reduced today by consumer law.
A basic principle of contract and international law.

term: Ex turpi causa non oritur actio
meaning: No action arises from a wrongful cause.
use: Courts will not help a person whose claim is based on an illegal act.
A person given power cannot pass it on without authority.

meaning: The welfare of the people is the supreme law.
use: Justifies State action in the public interest, such as police power.
Reflected in Article 20(1): no punishment under a law made after the act.

meaning: No one should be vexed twice for the same cause.
use: The idea behind double jeopardy in Article 20(2).
The right to bring a case. Relaxed in India for Public Interest Litigation.
When a court acts without a petition, e.g. taking notice of a news report.
An act outside the legal authority of a body is void.
Payment for work done when a contract is not fully performed.
A writ to produce a detained person before court to test the legality of detention.
A writ ordering a public authority to perform its legal duty.
A writ quashing an order of a lower court or tribunal acting without jurisdiction.
A writ asking a person to show by what right they hold a public office.
